bodyMarkdown:
## Definition

A degraded mode is an operational condition in which a system continues to function but with reduced capability. The reduction may result from a component fault, an input outside the designed normal range, a lost connection, or operating conditions that exceed designed parameters.

A degraded mode is not a complete failure. The system has not stopped functioning; it is operating with what remains available. A degraded mode is also distinct from an error, because an error is a momentary event requiring immediate correction, while a degraded mode may persist while users continue to make decisions and take actions.

## Meaning in Creative Navy documentation

Creative Navy documentation treats degraded mode as a design target for complex operational software. Sensors drift, connectivity drops, components reach operational limits, and hardware can fault during operation. In maritime, industrial, clinical, and embedded contexts, degraded conditions are treated as expected operating conditions that require explicit interface behaviour.

The design question is not only whether the system can keep running. The design question is whether the system can keep running while making the reduced capability visible, preserving critical work where possible, and avoiding a misleading operational picture.

## What degraded-mode design includes

Degraded-mode design includes degradation communication. The user must know that the system is operating in a degraded mode, and the interface must identify the specific degradation, such as the affected sensor, component, or capability. A generic system problem message is not enough when the operational consequence depends on which capability has been reduced.

Degraded-mode design includes residual capability communication. The user must know what the system can still reliably do. This includes which data remains valid, which functions remain available, and which decisions can still be made with confidence.

Degraded-mode design includes continued operation support. Critical functions must remain operable in degraded mode where possible, even at reduced quality. A navigation system that stops displaying all information when one sensor fails makes the remaining navigational decisions harder without gaining anything from the failed component.

Degraded-mode design includes transition visibility. Entry into and exit from degraded mode must be shown as state transitions. A silent transition into degraded mode produces the same failure pattern as silent degradation.

## Silent degradation is the critical degraded-mode failure

Silent degradation occurs when the system continues to present data that appears complete and reliable after an input, component, connection, or refresh path has been compromised. The interface still implies completeness, but the operational picture is partial or degraded.

Silent degradation is consequential because users have no interface signal that their decisions are being made from reduced information. In embedded systems, silent degradation can occur when a display shows stale or extrapolated sensor values without indication. In data systems, silent degradation can occur when a component fails to refresh and the display continues showing data that appears current.

## Degraded mode differs from error and complete failure

A degraded mode differs from an error because an error is a momentary event that requires correction, while a degraded mode may become a sustained operating condition. Users may need to keep working under degraded conditions rather than wait for the condition to clear.

A degraded mode differs from complete failure because the system still performs some function. The correct design response is not simply to stop interaction. The interface must explain what has changed, what remains reliable, and what operational constraints now apply.

A degraded mode also differs from a hidden data quality problem only when the system makes the state visible. If a system continues without communicating the degraded condition, the result is silent degradation rather than a designed degraded mode.

## Examples in practice

Elsner Elektronik / Cala Touch KNX treated sensor faults, calibration drift, and delayed sensor readings as degraded modes. The interface communicates each fault type specifically, distinguishes routine calibration drift from sensor failure, and continues controlling all remaining systems during a single-sensor fault. Firmware timing synchronisation addressed silent degradation by preventing displayed values from falling out of correspondence with current sensor readings.

Cox Marine cluster displays treated single-engine and multi-engine fault scenarios as degraded-mode scenarios during Concept Convergence. In a multi-engine configuration with one engine in fault, the vessel continues operating at reduced propulsion. The display must communicate which engines are operational and which are not, without creating ambiguity across the configuration.

Torqeedo maritime HMI treated storm conditions and sensor connectivity issues as degraded operating contexts. The sensor cadence synchronisation architecture was designed to prevent apparent data transitions during hardware disruptions, which is a silent degradation prevention problem.

Gexcon CFD simulation treated a simulation configuration with internally contradictory parameters as a degraded model state. The simulation can run, but the outputs are unreliable. The pre-run validation architecture addresses this by preventing the simulation from entering a silent-degradation output mode.

## KISPE Space treats degradation as seven independent axes

The KISPE Space material treats degraded state as a position on seven independent axes rather than as one overall mode. The axes are source transport, asset access, asset delivery, freshness, origin, operational condition, and local change state.

Source transport can be reachable, unreachable, or unknown. Asset access can be permitted, restricted, or not checked. Asset delivery can be available, failed, pending, or unknown. Freshness can be current, stale, or not assessed. Origin can be observed, device-measured, provider notice, forecast, or prediction. Operational condition can be favourable, unfavourable, unknown, or not applicable, and only where the source semantics support that classification. Local change state can be saved locally, queued, confirmed shared, or unresolved.

The rejected alternative in the KISPE Space material is one green-to-red health score. That alternative is compact, but it would make identical colours carry conflicting meanings across domains.

The KISPE Space material also rejects four shortcuts. Grey is not necessarily offline. Red is not necessarily inaccurate. An old observation is not automatically false. A nominal coverage footprint is not proof that a particular terminal is connected.

## Schone Airspace Group separates control-channel degradation from object health

Schone Airspace Group material shows that degradation can belong to the control channel independently of the controlled object. An aircraft in perfect health behind an unreliable link is degraded in a sense not covered by examples that concern equipment faults or process faults.

The path by which an instruction travels can become unreliable while the object at the far end remains healthy. The interface must report the unreliable path without asserting anything about the condition of the controlled object.

## Maritime VTS retained markers show marker-level silent degradation

In the maritime VTS engagement, the client is a European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations and waterway operators.

In the audited products, time of last observation sat behind secondary inspection. In a degraded state, a retained target could keep the same visual treatment as an updating one. The display did not reliably tell the operator whether a marker represented a current observation or a last known position, and an equipment view with no state data could read as an equipment view with no faults.

The designed response keeps a retained marker carrying its age and its source. This names silent degradation at the level of a single marker rather than only at system level.

## Evidence basis

The evidence basis is case-study material across maritime, industrial, clinical, embedded, simulation, space systems, airspace control, and maritime VTS contexts. The examples do not establish a universal taxonomy of all degraded modes. They show recurring design requirements for making reduced capability visible and actionable.

The examples should be kept in separate classes. Elsner Elektronik / Cala Touch KNX, Cox Marine, Torqeedo, and Gexcon concern equipment or process faults. KISPE Space adds degradation of information availability. Schone Airspace Group adds degradation of the control channel. These classes should not be blended into a single claim.

KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, and the maritime VTS engagement are not AI examples in this documentation. They do not include a model, inference, or recommendations.

## Boundaries and limits

A degraded mode should not be used as a synonym for any error message, any fault, or any system failure. The defining condition is continued operation with reduced capability.

A degraded mode should not be treated as adequately designed merely because the system continues running. If the interface does not communicate the specific degradation and the residual capability, users may still be acting under silent degradation.

The KISPE Space degraded-state material was specified against a synthetic fixture and was never executed. The product was built, but Creative Navy did not support the build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs.

Schone Airspace Group material concerns a product that was built and is in test, not deployed.

No KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, or maritime VTS material on this page establishes a safety, certification, or regulatory credential.

## Related pages

State visibility is closely related because degraded modes require the operating state to be visible rather than implied.

Transition clarity is closely related because entry into and exit from degraded mode must be communicated as state transitions.

Operational clarity and workflow robustness are related because users must understand what remains reliable and continue critical work within the reduced capability.
